implemented: Apple sessions carry the specific SocialIdentity id and original verified Apple proof timestamp; HTTP guards validate ownership and durable revocation state.
Session refresh preserves Apple identity/proof binding. Email-confirmed Apple linking mints a bound session instead of returning the unbound OTP token.
An additive SocialLoginChallenge.providerAuthenticatedAt migration preserves exact provider proof time across pending links; legacy pending Apple links fail closed.

Apple notifications validate RS256 signatures, fixed Anstoss audience/issuer and bounded event shape. The documented notification format without exp is accepted; foreign audiences and forged signatures are rejected.
Revocation markers advance monotonically under the same subject advisory lock as login/linking. Replays, delayed notifications and newer reauthorizations cannot reactivate old sessions.

Chat, events and live-match sockets use identity-scoped cross-replica disconnects, per-packet validation and periodic validation. Passive sockets are rechecked every 30 seconds with a 5-second query deadline; missed broadcasts are not claimed to revoke instantaneously.
Transport close during an unfinished namespace handshake removes listeners and prevents polling timer leaks.
Nest event listeners propagate adapter failures so notification delivery can be retried. Real EventEmitterModule tests cover all three gateway decorators.

Apple token verification is separated from authorization-code exchange. Acquisition holds the subject lock and journals encrypted credentials before the separate business transaction; exact journal ownership is consumed atomically with the account/link write.

SocialIdentity.providerAuthenticatedAt prevents older abandoned credentials from replacing newer ones. Unknown-freshness legacy linking fails without consuming the pending credential; a fresh live exchange can initialize legacy freshness.
Cleanup and acquisition share subject locking with a 2-second lock timeout, leaving time for bounded provider requests before the transaction deadline.
Persistent cleanupNextAttemptAt claims rotate deferred and failed identities/grants across worker restarts. Conditional claims prevent concurrent workers from processing the same eligible row.
Old revocation markers are pruned only after their identity is absent, with post-lock ownership and age rechecks. Required active-identity markers cannot starve removable markers.

Expired, missing or consumed linking tickets return OAUTH_LINK_EXPIRED (410). Revoked Apple link proofs also require a fresh provider sign-in. Mobile recovery clears the stale ticket and offers an explicit sign-in-method restart without silently falling back to email verification.

Wrong OTP, transient network errors and rate limits retain the pending link for retry. Synchronous request guards prevent overlapping resend, verification and navigation actions; recovery preserves email and invite context.

grantDatabaseCoverage: Business rollback preserves the encrypted grant; successful ownership consumes its exact journal
Newer grants transfer while older, equal-revoked and pre-revocation proofs cannot overwrite them
Actual provider exchange races cleanup and concurrent account deletion under the shared subject lock
Successful provider revocation followed by a database rollback preserves durable retry state
Legacy link failure preserves its pending credential
An eligible tail progresses behind 100 retained rows after worker restart
Concurrent workers cannot claim the same due grant
Lock contention fails before contacting the provider
Provider failure retry respects its persisted schedule after restart
Only unused old markers are pruned
validation.scopeCaveat: Tests exercise current review-checkout code, simulated providers, generated test signatures and isolated PostgreSQL. They do not prove Apple notification configuration, native provider login, locked-phone delivery or billing-store lifecycle delivery.

remainingAuthGates: Apple exchange and PostgreSQL cannot share an atomic commit. Process termination or response/persistence failure after a provider grant is issued remains an indeterminate external-state gap; no exactly-once guarantee. Login fails closed and local failures emit sanitized diagnostics, but live operational recovery and monitoring still need verification.
Legacy unknown-freshness grants are retained rather than blindly revoked or overwritten. Verify fresh-login recovery and account-deletion cleanup in the final native/provider flow.

Expired-link recovery is locally implemented, regression tested and independently reviewed; native light/dark, large-text and genuine provider-flow validation remain pending. The refreshed full suites include the four mobile and two API database recovery regressions.
